projects.title: ANT Meta Bots – ML-Powered Options Trading Platform
projects.description: An end-to-end algorithmic trading platform that generates ML-based signals and autonomously executes and manages options trades in real time.
highlights: Built Lorentzian k-NN based ML system for generating LONG/SHORT signals from futures data
Automated options execution with dynamic ATM strike selection and Delta Exchange API integration
Designed unified async engine handling signal processing and trade lifecycle at 1-second intervals
Implemented full trade management: TP, SL, trailing stops, re-entry, and session-based force-close
Handled full trade lifecycle across signal → execution → monitoring → exit with strict state control and zero double-execution guarantees

architecture: End-to-end pipeline from futures data → ML signal generation → options execution
Dual live data feeds for futures (signal) and options (execution monitoring)
Multi-bot architecture supporting independent strategy instances
Session-based lifecycle management with controlled trade isolation
engineering: Unified async Watchdog engine replacing multi-component architecture
Fill verification pipeline with fallback and emergency handling
Persistent state using SQLite with automatic recovery
React dashboard with WebSocket-based real-time monitoring and control

insights.problem: Maintaining independence between multiple real-time system layers while still enabling meaningful interaction between them.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Each subsystem (data manager, live feed, signal generator, trade monitor) had its own lifecycle, data format, and execution model, making synchronization and communication extremely complex.
failure_points: State desynchronization across async systems
Duplicate trade execution under rapid signal changes
Inconsistent data handling across subsystems
insights.real_world_behavior: System handled multiple bots, each consuming live futures and options data independently, while executing trades in real time without double execution or state corruption.
insights.what_i_learned: True system reliability comes from controlling state transitions, not just generating better signals.

metrics.scale: Supports multiple bots, live feeds, and signal streams concurrently
metrics.latency: 1-second execution cycle across all core systems
metrics.throughput: Continuous async processing of signals, trades, and live feeds
metrics.impact: Fully automated end-to-end trading lifecycle with zero manual intervention

projects.title: Telegram Signal Distribution System – Event-Driven Trade Execution Pipeline
projects.description: An event-driven trading infrastructure that ingests unstructured Telegram signals, validates them, and distributes them to individual MetaTrader accounts via a pull-based execution model.
highlights: Built event-driven pipeline: Telegram ingestion → validation → per-user signal queues → MT5 execution
Designed pull-based execution system where MT5 clients poll signals to avoid push-related failures
Implemented per-account in-memory queues enabling isolated signal delivery at scale
Handled real-time signal parsing, validation, modification, and cancellation flows
Deployed production system on AWS EC2 with systemd-managed service lifecycle

architecture: Event-driven system bridging Telegram (signal source) and MetaTrader (execution layer)
Producer-consumer model using in-memory queues (ConcurrentHashMap + ConcurrentLinkedQueue)
Pull-based delivery via REST polling endpoint for MT5 clients
Stateless execution layer on MT5 with server-controlled signal lifecycle
No frontend — full system operated via Telegram bot commands
engineering: Regex-based signal parsing and strict validation before execution
TTL-based signal expiry (10s for market orders, 10min for pending orders)
Admin state machine for multi-step user provisioning via Telegram chat
Monthly automated JSON backups via scheduled jobs
Broker-specific symbol normalization inside MT5 EA for cross-broker compatibility
system_design: Solved unreliable push delivery by designing a pull-based execution model
Ensured per-user isolation using independent signal queues per MetaTrader ID
Handled signal lifecycle events: CREATE → MODIFY → CANCEL
Designed idempotent polling mechanism preventing duplicate trade execution
Balanced real-time delivery with system simplicity (no external message broker)

insights.problem: Distributing real-time trading signals from an unreliable external source (Telegram) to multiple independent trading accounts without duplication or loss.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Telegram messages are unstructured and execution happens on independent MT5 terminals, requiring strict validation, synchronization, and delivery guarantees.
tradeoffs: In-memory queues vs persistent message brokers
Strict validation vs flexible signal formats
failure_points: Duplicate execution due to repeated polling
Invalid signals causing incorrect trades
Signal delays causing stale execution
Client desynchronization across multiple MT5 instances
insights.real_world_behavior: System continuously listens to Telegram groups, parses valid trading signals, distributes them to all registered accounts, and ensures each MT5 client executes trades independently via polling.
insights.what_i_learned: In distributed systems, delivery guarantees and execution control matter more than raw speed — especially when external systems are unreliable.

metrics.scale: Supports multiple MT5 accounts with isolated signal pipelines
metrics.latency: Near real-time ingestion with ~10 second polling execution cycle
metrics.throughput: Continuous event-driven signal processing and distribution
metrics.impact: Enabled automated trade execution across multiple accounts from a single signal source

personality.approach: Design reliable pipelines around unreliable external systems
personality.strength: Building event-driven systems with controlled execution flow
personality.edge: Choosing simplicity (polling + in-memory queues) over over-engineered infrastructure

projects.title: Quant Discovery Pipeline – Automated Strategy Mining System
projects.description: A high-performance, multi-layer pipeline that discovers statistically validated trading strategies by simulating millions of trades and learning patterns from enriched market data.
highlights: Simulates millions of SL/TP trade combinations using Numba-accelerated engines
Generates 300+ market context features including indicators, patterns, and regime signals
Supports dual output: human-readable strategy rules or machine-learned XGBoost models
Processes massive datasets efficiently using sharded Parquet pipelines and multiprocessing

architecture: Layered data pipeline (Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum → Diamond) separating compute concerns
Bronze layer performs exhaustive trade simulation across SL/TP grids using JIT acceleration
Silver layer enriches trades with indicators, ZigZag S/R, and session-aware features
Gold layer applies relational normalization and rolling statistical scaling
Platinum layer splits into Decision Tree rule mining or ML dataset generation
Diamond layer trains XGBoost models using full-memory or streaming datasets
engineering: Numba JIT used to accelerate inner simulation loops to near-C performance
Multiprocessing architecture for parallel chunk-based execution
Parquet-based storage replacing CSV for high-throughput I/O
Config-driven pipeline enabling full system tuning without code changes
Streaming dataset support for low-RAM environments using iterative loading

insights.problem: Extracting statistically reliable trading strategies from massive raw OHLCV datasets.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Trade simulation, feature engineering, and ML training each require different compute models and memory strategies.
tradeoffs: Full-memory training vs streaming dataset training
Precomputed datasets vs flexibility in experimentation
failure_points: Out-of-memory crashes during large dataset processing
I/O bottlenecks with traditional CSV workflows
Feature explosion leading to inefficient ML training
insights.real_world_behavior: Pipeline processes large-scale historical market data, simulates trade outcomes, and extracts statistically significant strategies for real trading environments.
insights.what_i_learned: At scale, data architecture and pipeline design matter more than model complexity.

metrics.scale: Processes tens of crores of rows across multiple pipeline stages
metrics.latency: Reduced full pipeline runtime from hours to minutes via parallelization
metrics.throughput: Parallel multi-layer processing with chunked data flow
metrics.impact: Enables large-scale quantitative strategy discovery on limited hardware

personality.approach: Design pipelines that align computation with data scale instead of forcing generic solutions
personality.strength: Building high-performance systems under real hardware constraints
personality.edge: Combining quantitative finance, ML, and systems engineering into one unified pipeline

projects.title: Stella – Transactional E-Commerce Backend System
projects.description: A production-style e-commerce backend implementing a fully transactional order lifecycle, stateless authentication, and strict separation of system layers.
highlights: Designed a full transactional order lifecycle with Razorpay two-phase payment verification
Implemented stateless JWT authentication enforced via Spring Security filter chain
Built complete buyer-seller ecosystem with strict role-based access control
Handled real-world flows: cart → order creation → payment → verification → fulfillment
Designed layered architecture with strict separation between controllers, services, and repositories

architecture: Layered monolithic architecture (Controller → Service → Repository → DB)
Stateless backend using JWTAuthenticationFilter and SecurityContext
Strict DTO-based API boundary to isolate database models from external exposure
External integrations: Razorpay (payments), SMTP (email verification), filesystem (media storage)
Two-step verification system for account activation and sensitive updates
engineering: Two-phase payment system ensuring orders are only confirmed after signature verification
Order state machine (creating → created → paid → processing → shipped → delivered)
Global exception handling with structured API error responses
Multipart file handling with controlled upload limits and validation
Repository-driven data access using Spring Data JPA with zero raw SQL
system_design: Ensured consistency between payment gateway state and internal order state
Designed idempotent payment callback handling to avoid duplicate processing
Handled trust boundaries between client, backend, and Razorpay API
Balanced stateless authentication with persistent user/session data
Maintained separation between buyer and seller flows without duplicating logic

insights.problem: Designing a reliable e-commerce backend where payments, orders, and user actions remain consistent across external systems.
insights.why_it_was_hard: The system interacts with external services (Razorpay, SMTP) while maintaining internal consistency, requiring strict validation, state management, and trust boundaries.
tradeoffs: Stateless JWT auth vs server-side session control
failure_points: Payment success but order not updated due to callback failure
Duplicate payment callbacks causing inconsistent order state
Unauthorized access due to improper role validation
File upload vulnerabilities without strict validation
insights.real_world_behavior: Users register, verify via email, add products to cart, create orders, complete payment via Razorpay, and the system validates and updates order state before triggering fulfillment.
insights.what_i_learned: In real systems, correctness of state transitions matters more than feature completeness — especially when money is involved.

metrics.scale: Supports full buyer-seller ecosystem with multiple concurrent users
metrics.latency: Low-latency REST APIs with stateless request handling
metrics.throughput: Handles concurrent order creation, payment callbacks, and cart operations
metrics.impact: Implements a complete real-world e-commerce transaction lifecycle

personality.approach: Design systems around real-world flows and failure cases, not just APIs
personality.strength: Building reliable transactional systems with external integrations
personality.edge: Thinking in terms of state transitions and trust boundaries

projects.title: Elastic DCA Engine – Deterministic Trading State Machine
projects.description: A server-centric trading engine that transforms MetaTrader into a stateless execution layer, enabling deterministic grid trading, real-time control, and fault-tolerant trade lifecycle management.
highlights: Built a server-authoritative trading engine where MetaTrader acts as a stateless executor
Designed deterministic execution pipeline processing every tick into validated trade actions
Implemented dual independent trading systems (buy/sell) with isolated state machines
Achieved real-time synchronization across trading terminal, backend engine, and UI

architecture: Server-centric architecture with FastAPI controlling all trading logic
State machine (DcaEngine) managing full trade lifecycle in memory
Pull-based execution model using action queues to avoid MT5 context conflicts
WebSocket-driven UI streaming full system state every second
engineering: Tick-based event pipeline with deterministic step-by-step execution
Session-based trade isolation using unique identifiers for each cycle
Automatic orphan trade detection and cleanup mechanisms
Database-backed preset system with strict runtime mutation rules
system_design: Solved synchronization between independent systems (MT5 ↔ backend)
Designed resilient execution despite network delays or missed ticks
Handled real-world failure cases like zombie trades and state mismatch
Balanced real-time responsiveness with system stability

insights.problem: Maintaining a consistent and reliable trading state across an external execution system (MetaTrader) and a backend engine.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Both systems operate independently, causing desynchronization, incorrect PnL mapping, and trade duplication risks.
tradeoffs: Strict state validation vs system flexibility
failure_points: Incorrect trade-to-row mapping due to comment mismatch
Desync between server state and live positions
Race conditions in rapid tick environments
insights.real_world_behavior: The system continuously processes live ticks, validates state, generates actions, and reconciles results from the trading terminal.
insights.what_i_learned: Reliable distributed systems require shared contracts and deterministic state transitions, not assumptions.

metrics.scale: Runs parallel independent trading systems (buy & sell grids)
metrics.latency: Processes trading decisions every second (tick-driven loop)
metrics.impact: Transforms an unreliable trading flow into a deterministic system

personality.approach: Convert unreliable external systems into deterministic pipelines using strict state control
personality.strength: Designing real-time systems that stay consistent under uncertainty
personality.edge: Thinking in state machines, not scripts

projects.title: Rubik's Cube Solver — State-Space Search & Optimization Engine
projects.description: A high-performance Rubik’s Cube solving engine that models the cube as a constrained state space and applies a hybrid deterministic-stochastic search strategy using CFOP.
highlights: Designed a state-space search engine evaluating 10k+ candidate solutions per solve
Implemented multi-start optimization across 6 cube orientations
Built hybrid deterministic (OLL/PLL) and stochastic (F2L randomization) solver pipeline
Developed custom move-optimization engine reducing redundant operations
Consistently produces near-optimal solutions (<42 moves) in ~2 seconds

architecture: 3D cube state representation using vector-based model
CFOP pipeline (Cross → F2L → OLL → PLL) as modular solving stages
Multi-start search across cube orientations for global optimization
Solution vector compression via rule-based optimizer
engineering: Handles thousands of candidate solution paths per execution
ANSI-based CLI visualization for step-by-step solving
Designed without external libraries using pure STL
Built with extensibility for alternative solving strategies

insights.problem: Efficiently solving a combinatorial puzzle with a massive state space (~43 quintillion states).
insights.why_it_was_hard: Balancing solution optimality with computation time while modeling cube rotations accurately.
tradeoffs: Optimality vs speed (CFOP vs exhaustive search)
failure_points: Initial brute-force approaches were computationally infeasible
State transition bugs caused incorrect cube states
insights.real_world_behavior: System evaluates thousands of candidate solutions and selects the shortest valid sequence in real time.
insights.what_i_learned: Even problems with massive state spaces can be solved efficiently by constraining the search space with domain-specific heuristics instead of brute force.

system_design: Designed hybrid deterministic-stochastic solving pipeline
Used multi-start search to approximate global optimum
Balanced search space exploration vs computation time
Separated state mutation from solution tracking for correctness

projects.title: Lorentzian ML Engine – Cross-Platform Signal Generation System
projects.description: A cross-language implementation of a Lorentzian distance-based KNN trading strategy, designed as a reusable signal-generation engine for real-time trading systems.
highlights: Implemented Lorentzian-distance KNN model for financial time-series prediction
Built cross-language parity across Python, MQL5, and Pine Script
Designed hybrid ML + kernel regression signal generation pipeline
Used as core signal engine in production trading systems (ANT Meta Bots)
Processes 2750+ candle history with multi-phase training and real-time inference

architecture: Three parallel implementations: Pine Script (reference), MQL5 (live indicator), Python (core engine)
Self-contained ring buffer storing full historical state per bar
Three-phase pipeline: Warmup → Training → Backtest/Live prediction
Modular feature + kernel + filter pipeline for extensibility
engineering: Custom Lorentzian distance metric replacing Euclidean for time-series similarity
KNN search optimized with modulo filtering and bounded neighbor set
Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression for trend confirmation
Zero external ML dependencies — full algorithm implemented from scratch
system_design: Ensured deterministic cross-language parity for validation across platforms
Designed for streaming real-time data (incremental candle processing)
Separated signal generation from execution layer (clean system boundary)
Built reusable API layer for integration into trading bots and pipelines

insights.problem: Generating reliable trading signals from noisy financial time-series data without relying on heavy ML frameworks.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Financial data is non-linear, noisy, and non-stationary, making traditional distance metrics and models unreliable without careful feature engineering and filtering.
tradeoffs: Deterministic pipeline vs adaptive ML models
failure_points: Initial Euclidean distance produced unstable neighbor selection
Feature scaling inconsistencies affected prediction quality
Cross-language mismatch bugs during early porting stages
insights.real_world_behavior: Engine continuously processes incoming candles, updates internal state, performs KNN search over historical patterns, and emits directional signals in real time.
insights.what_i_learned: Building reliable ML systems for real-time use requires controlling data representation and algorithm behavior more than model complexity.

metrics.latency: Real-time inference per candle with optimized search
metrics.impact: Serves as core signal engine powering live trading systems

personality.strength: Designing mathematical systems that work in real-time environments
personality.edge: Bridging theory (ML) with production-grade execution systems
